instructions:
# actor-turn-core-01: construct a coherent recovery action controller

Parent/base commit: `2f0f534e8311ee597e516b11c2afca1bbf608060`.
Base bot: `leader_party_tuned`.
Allowed output: `bots/pi_actor-turn-core-01/` only, including tests and
IMPLEMENTATION.md. Do not edit other bots, SDK, maps, bridge or tools. This is a
new decision-core construction branch, not a port of rejected candidates.

## Objective and complete scope

The user explicitly requested considering a substantial bot rebuild after many
individually sensible fixes failed strength. We selected a two-stage decision
core: one economic-task owner feeding one action controller. Your job is the
first complete slice: replace recovery/escape turn execution with a bounded
planner/executor that owns ordinary movement, dash sequences, defensive followup,
active recall decisions and health-recall initiation. Original high-level intent
selection is a temporary adapter. Economic selection will be replaced in a
subsequent dependent job; do not implement it now.

Intermediate construction is NOT required to win against champion. It must be
legal, bounded, observable and actually express the specified sequences. The
completed combined design will receive a separately frozen strength evaluation.
Do not optimize this job by removing a required capability to preserve old play.

No new draft/shop thresholds, gold-recall trigger, economic utility, team
communication, tentatively recalling at full health, whole-map tactical search,
or private SDK imports. Preserve existing camp/bank/navigation behavior outside
the recovery adapter for this stage. The new recovery implementation must NOT
fall back to old `retreat` or risk-masked `move_to` as its decision engine.

## Evidence (self-contained; PC cache is not on Pi)

Current engine3 and C++ SDK contracts are compatible with this base. Original
`move_to` demands ordinary movement and a risk-masked walking route BEFORE
considering dash. Its dash candidates also use that risk mask and it returns
immediately after success. Escape then calls defend/fight but never reconsiders
health recall in the same turn. These coupled constraints cannot reproduce:

1. Original Swirl B37 Ren7: `(21,15)`,120/900HP, no bag, ready nonexclusive
   range2 effectless dash. All legal ordinary moves have current basic exposure
   >=60. `(19,15)` is native-legal and visible, with physical midpoint `(20,15)`
   empty and current exposure0. Enemy reaction range+1 still covers the landing.
   Actual original ends37–40 without moving, HP unchanged. This proves an option,
   not saved damage. Native absence of `(19,17)`/`(20,17)` is a negative control.
2. Original Swirl A30 Heart0: `(18,13)`,230/1000HP, no bag, ready nonexclusive
   range2/radius1/modifier1.5/stun1 dash. Awake camp26 `(20,14)`,range4,Strength60
   covers every ordinary move. Native-legal dash to `(16,15)` via empty visible
   `(17,14)` leaves exposure60, but adjacent visible vacant `(15,15)` has0.
   The entire3x3 landing-effect footprint at `(16,15)` is visible and has no
   enemy/camp. Other nearby landings hit passive members of a sleeping group,
   so pre-action threat geometry alone is invalid for those. Actual original
   walks/rolls over30, shields31, walks/rolls over32, HP unchanged. The compound
   sequence is a counterfactual to validate, not an already executed original.
3. Leader Pantheon Ren245 actually dashes `(38,20)`→`(36,18)` via empty visible
   `(37,19)` then walks `(35,17)`, exposure60→20→0, starts recall and returns250.
   Both movements coexist with its nonexclusive dash. This establishes capability,
   not leader source policy or the optimal threshold.
4. Original Heart A37 moves `(18,7)`→`(19,6)` at230/1000HP. Before moving a foe is
   visible; afterward none, no awake camp covers it, no channel/stun/restriction.
   It ends37, recalls38 unchanged, returns43, heals by44. B40 similarly moves
   `(22,15)`→`(23,14)` at220/1000HP, recalls41, returns46, healed by47.
   Starting committed health recall after reaching that safe local state is a
   testable one-turn saving. Both have0gems; carriers need separate controls.
5. Original Restricted Marcella126 has active recall timer2,415/1200HP at(24,0).
   Sole visible foe Vesper is12tiles away, zero current/reaction-range exposure,
   no damaging awake camp. It cancels, moves(25,0), reaches own spawn(26,1)127,
   heals and resumes128. Preserving unchanged timer2 would arrive128 and heal
   at its end under documented channel timing. Do not preserve every channel
   indiscriminately; compare a currently known clear home path with its timer.

All local probes preserve exact native event prefixes/endpoints. Hidden state,
private original task/stack and counterfactual wins are not observed. Historical
reliable/complete rewrites and recent wake-veto/rank-reuse patches lost strength;
do not copy their entire policies. New observation cost is a concrete risk.

## Module interface and integration

Design one small public recovery execution interface consuming current intent,
memory and a backend, returning an explicit outcome. At minimum distinguish
channeling (not yet arrived), reached spawn (healing not yet observed), recovered,
partial actions, blocked attempt, no improving plan, incomplete resource work,
and stale epoch. Pure plan selection can be an internal
seam exercised by recorded/scenario scenes. Production SDK and scripted test
adapters must exercise the SAME controller, not duplicated decision code.

The controller owns its scene values and executed-action history. A retained
SDK handle or reference to `observe()` is not an immutable observation. Do not
store a future action across turns. Original `Memory.recovering` uses low0.35 /
high0.55 hysteresis; retain those thresholds as an initial intent model. Update
the health latch from fresh observations after actions as well as at entry.

Route original `State::escape` into this controller, with explicit health-
recovery vs evasion intent. Also route `State::recall` with health recovery into
it, so active channels and fresh recovery share an owner. Preserve the old
gold-only recall branch and its triggers outside this adapter. Preserve original
decide ordering, including dead/tribute/teleport and spawn-defense handling; do
not add a spawn-healing override before danger or existing recall.
The exact routing test is all `State::escape`, or `State::recall` with the fresh
`Memory.recovering` health latch set; do not use `Facts.recovery`, which includes
gold. Existing recall origin does not override this test. Gold-only evasion
cannot start the health footer unless new observed damage activates the latch.
Keep task abandonment/carrier release on actual escape entry, but avoid
unconditionally cancelling an existing recall before the controller decides.

Integrate final returned state without allowing old post-dispatch ward or other
actions after a new channel. Do not falsify bank/capture/progress counters to
make outcomes look productive. Distinguish movement from recovery completion.

## SDK, scene and geometry contracts

- A self state provides separate `can_move` and `can_cast`. A nonexclusive dash
  can be proposed when normal movement is spent. `ability::is_ready` does not
  cover all channel, restriction or destination checks.
  Explicit dash guards are alive, not completed/channeling, `can_cast`,
  cooldown0, no move or cast buff restriction, current actor/life/epoch and
  supported metadata. Normal-move allowance is independent for nonexclusive
  dash; recheck after every action or channel cancellation.
- `ability::valid_tiles()` is RANGE ONLY, not a legal destination mask. Do not
  use visualizer functions, private imports or assumed bit layouts in the bot.
- Initial supported dash envelope is range<=2. Use physical eight-neighbor
  paths with every intermediate/landing in bounds, currently visible and free
  of walls, holes, altars, enemy spawn, champion/camp/teleport occupancy. Clear
  self's actual origin. This established walking-connected physical subset is
  conservative but admits the three required witnesses. Do NOT add tactical
  threat masks to physical reachability. Cross-hole/occupied overflight is
  explicitly unsupported initially. Unsupported metadata takes an explicit
  non-dash fallback, not guessed legality or silent range truncation.
- Capture one owned local dynamic scene per observation/action epoch; use
  public bitboard exports to scalar occupancy/visibility. `is_set()` itself
  is a host call, so no SDK getter/bitboard call belongs inside endpoint/ranking
  loops. Static geometry and group membership can be cached once per life/map.
- Build camp-handle→group membership from `World`'s already cached groups.
  `camp::camp_group()` reloads metadata; never call it per endpoint. Visible
  camp live values must be captured once, only when relevant. Missing or hidden
  camp information is unknown. Fresh `camp.state()==dead` is valid only when
  that camp's last tile is visible; absence from vision is not death evidence.
- Capture visible current basic threats as scalar position/range/Strength.
  Keep current exposure and visible enemy range+1 response exposure separate.
  Both are geometric risk features, not predicted HP loss. Do not subtract
  shields, assume enemy cooldowns, or pretend a zero score guarantees safety.

## Conservative landing effects

Effectless dash needs no effect scan. For a dash with damage or stun, require
its entire in-bounds effect footprint visible. Enemy contacts with unsupported
retaliation/passive effects are `effect_unknown` and excluded. For every hit
living camp, including passive or already awake members, identify its group.
Require fresh live or fresh dead evidence for every member of hit groups;
otherwise exclude that candidate as `effect_unknown`.

For supported positive-damage contacts add all known living asleep damaging
members of hit groups to that candidate's threat geometry at full Strength.
Retain existing awake threats. Do not subtract predicted kills or beneficial
stuns. Cache group/effect results for each landing, never scan SDK members for
each continuation. Stun-only uncertain wake effects may be excluded explicitly.

This conservative model may reject original Heart599 even though stun made its
actual dash temporarily safe. It should penalize864/985's wider wake and accept
HeartA30's no-hit `(16,15)` and Ren's effectless dashes. Leader Heart147's valid
hole-crossing dash is deliberately outside this initial subset. Report these
limitations; do not claim full engine effect simulation.

## Bounded planning policy to implement

Generate stay, one ordinary step, one dash, dash→step and step→dash when the
captured allowances support them. At most417 raw choices for range2 before
deduplication. One cast and one ordinary move maximum in these motion sequences.
Exclusive-with-movement dash sequencing is unsupported unless exact consumed-
movement history proves legality; do not infer it from `!can_move` alone.

Each plan has a terminal risk and every action-prefix risk. Exclude a motion
plan if any prefix's conservative current basic exposure exceeds the origin's
current exposure. Intermediate exposure need NOT be zero: Heart60→60→0 and
Ren60→20→0 must remain representable. Exclude unknown effects. Among supported
plans rank lexicographically:

1. terminal current basic exposure (lower);
2. terminal enemy response exposure at range+1 (lower);
3. terminal physical home distance (lower; unreachable stays a distinct value);
4. terminal distance from nearest visible enemy (higher, if any);
5. worst action-prefix current exposure (lower);
6. number of issued motion actions (lower), then stable coordinate/action ties.

These are initial policy hypotheses, not fitted damage predictors. Include stay
so no improving plan does not force a move. A static physical home-distance
field may be computed once and cached, via public SDK and existing shared field
budget; it must not contain dynamic risk/occupancy. Defer initialization that
is incomplete; do not mark partial field data valid. Use full
`distance_field::compute` from own spawn and export once to owned scalar data,
not origin-stopped `compute_to` cached as a whole-map result. A fully completed
static-only field/export may be retained even if initialization spans an epoch;
discard the dynamic scene/plan and return stale for this dispatch. This avoids
restarting the same expensive static work forever. Until the field is complete,
return initialization-deferred and issue no model-dependent action. No tactical
distance field per candidate or per continuation.

Execute only the FIRST action of the chosen plan, then refresh/replan from
observed state and remaining allowances. At most two successful motion actions,
at most one dash attempt and one ordinary move attempt in the controller turn;
a failed hidden-blocker attempt stops motion rather than retrying indefinitely.
The executed first action survives if refresh/second action is deferred or
rejected. Return partial completion explicitly. Never continue the predicted
second action without fresh allowance, geometry, effects and epoch checks.

## Channels and compatible defensive actions

For an existing recall, compare preserving it with recovery movement BEFORE
cancelling. If present and response exposure are zero, preserve it unless a
currently visible clear path reaches own spawn in <=remaining_timer ordinary
steps, all at zero current/response exposure. A bounded local BFS up to5steps
is sufficient for this exception; use scalar scene data and a shared work cap.
It is a snapshot-based time estimate, not guaranteed future safety. The timer2 /
two-step Restricted fixture must choose cancellation and the first safe step.
Current channel flags suppress ordinary action permissions. The faster-home
comparison uses the scalar physical path and known same-turn movement history,
not channel-blocked `can_move` as proof that walking after cancellation is
impossible. After cancellation refresh and require actual live move permission;
if it is unavailable, return partial/cancelled-wait rather than invent a move.
When cancellation selects this faster-home route, execute its first safe step,
mark this turn as homeward recovery, and suppress new recall initiation for the
rest of this turn. Reconsider from fresh state next turn; retain no future
action. If that selected step becomes blocked, report the failed/partial result
rather than switching silently back to a newly started channel in this turn.
If no such safe faster route and no current/response threat, finish the channel
without voluntary cancellation merely because a distant enemy is visible.

If threatened, cancel only through valid current channel permissions, refresh,
then plan. Cancellation itself is an action/revision and must be bounded once.
Never cancel tribute/teleport here. If no motion is possible, retain an explicit
defensive/wait outcome; absence of a path is not recovery success.

The controller must also own compatible post-motion defense/counterattack. You
may retain the original shield/heal/travel-combat policy as an explicit internal
adapter, with its action allowance/epoch/invalidation contract reviewed and
reported. It must not make movement decisions, start/cancel channels, or be
called repeatedly until it acts. Refresh afterward before health/channel
decisions. Do not let an opaque legacy call resume and then issue another stale
controller action. If extracting primitive guarded actions is simpler, do so,
but document the retained/changed policy and preserve camp-service combat.

At a fresh no-channel recovery state, first allow a supported plan that reaches
own spawn immediately. Otherwise, after motion/defense, begin committed health
recall only when the original health latch remains set, self is alive outside
spawn, HP remains below high threshold, no visible foe, no covering damaging
awake camp, no current exposure, and permissions below pass. Gold alone never
activates this footer. Existing safe health recovery may start recall without
motion. Do not add full-health tentative recall or always cancel next turn.

Recall permissions: alive, no stun, no existing channel, not completed turn,
no recall already started this turn, same actor/life/round, reserve available.
There is no generic SDK recall-restriction bit. `restrictions==0` alone is NOT
sufficient. A failed/cancelled earlier recall must not cause a second start in
the same turn. Recheck exact permissions/epoch immediately before issuance and
fresh state afterward. Starting recall does not imply eventual arrival/healing.

## Work, fuel, stale state and errors

Use the existing TurnBudget round and total field budget, Config::reserve5000
and field_admission30000 as INITIAL guards, not measured cost guarantees. Keep
all dynamic capture and planning bounded; declare record/query/candidate caps
in code and report them. If data collection exceeds a cap, return incomplete;
never ignore remaining threats and label the partial model safe. Precompute
local features from scalar records instead of repeated live queries. Bound
fresh captures to initial, after channel cancellation, after each successful
motion, and after defensive actions as needed; reuse unchanged scenes.

Check epochs around each host-query batch and action. A suspension can resume
inside a call next round. After rollover, discard the plan and partial scene,
issue no stale action, and return stale/partial. Do not restart an unbounded
controller loop in the same dispatch. Do not promise that a fuel check makes
multiple actions atomic. Current-round unexpected SDK errors remain reported;
do not blanket-catch them as successful recovery. Existing outer stale handling
may remain, but deliberate hidden live queries are forbidden.
Incomplete/stale outcomes bypass all further defense, recall-footer and optional
ward work in the caller, including when the controller already performed a
partial action. A no-improving-motion outcome can still permit fresh guarded
defense/health recall; it is distinct from incomplete observation or computation.

Prefer counters in returned outcomes and compile-time optional diagnostics.
Default release must not print a per-action trace or run extra debug queries.
If diagnostics are provided, state precisely which build is measured; disabled
diagnostics must be compile-time absent. PC will measure real fuel/rollover and
cap hits rather than accept a theoretical fuel claim.

## Required tests and report

Tests must call the actual new controller/planner interface through a scripted
adapter. Include inherited ordinary source syntax checks. At minimum:

- Ren pure dash with walking spent; walking path rejected by risk but physically
  valid; blocked midpoint/visible occupant/teleport/map edge negative controls.
- Heart no-hit dash→walk; leader Ren partial60→20→0; step→dash; unsupported
  exclusive metadata; known and hidden failed destinations; successful first
  action then unavailable/rejected/stale second action.
- Full/partial visibility, passive hit waking remote group member, awake hit
  waking asleep sibling, unknown sibling, fresh dead member, duplicate hit
  groups; beneficial kill/stun not invented; no-hit/effectless positive controls.
- A37/B40 health-recall footer, enemy visible outside immediate threat still
  blocks fresh footer, combat-healing releases latch, spawn arrival, no-health
  gold-only intent, active tribute/teleport, dead/stunned/completed/already-started
  recall, cancelled recall, health carrier preservation.
- Active safe recall retained, threatened recall cancelled once, Restricted
  timer2/2-step faster-home exception, obstructed/exposed/unknown home path stays.
- Rollover during scene capture, planning prerequisite, cancellation, first
  action, refresh and final preflight: no stale second action; completed work
  accounted once. Caps yield incomplete, not falsely safe or completed.
- Rank deterministic ties; stay retained when nothing improves; fields shared;
  per-candidate host call count zero; no recovery fallback to originalretreat.
- Production intent adapter routes only selected states, preserves ordinary
  camp/bank behavior and does not perform optional ward after starting recall.

IMPLEMENTATION.md must enumerate actual changed files, interface/ownership,
ordering, limits, operation caps, tested assertions and unverified engine/fuel
claims. Include runnable tests and exact commands. Do not claim competitive
improvement. PC will independently review, build current SDK, run a frozen
8-game construction panel (Swirl/Lanes/Elkring/Guardians,both sides vsC02), and
inspect errors, action sequences, recovery, delivery and fuel. No automatic80,
no uploads, no ranked change. Subsequent economic-core work depends on a
reviewed commit and these construction findings, not a standalone win threshold.
implementation_report:
# actor-turn-core-01 implementation

Base: `2f0f534e8311ee597e516b11c2afca1bbf608060`, cloned `leader_party_tuned`.
This is a recovery-controller construction experiment. There is no competitive
improvement claim. No tournaments, uploads, ranked changes, commits or pushes
were performed. All edits are inside this candidate directory.

## Hypothesis and actual change

A single owner of recovery actions can express physical dash escapes, two-action
motion sequences, and immediate committed health recall without depending on a
risk-masked walking route. Replanning after each action should make these
sequences explicit while keeping stale observations and unknown landing effects
out of subsequent decisions. These are policy/construction hypotheses, not
predictions of prevented damage or wins.

Read: the current leader-party state-machine and configuration-tuning documents,
the strategy overview, GameRules action/destination/channel timing contracts,
and the checkout's public `sdk/cpp/cambc.h` interfaces for states, restrictions,
buffs, dash metadata, bitboard export, fields, camps and cached groups.

Changed inherited files:

- `src/bot.h`: owns persistent recovery runtime and includes its public adapter.
- `src/bot.cpp`: routes exactly every `State::escape`, or `State::recall` with
  fresh `Memory.recovering`, into the controller. Removes the old escape execution.
  Escape abandonment/carrier release remain; cancellation belongs to the controller.
  Integrates channeling/healing state and genuine motion/defer counters; released
  recovery returns to explore intent for the next dispatch, unfinished recovery
  keeps escape intent. It then
  returns without optional ward or another dispatch. Bank/capture/progress and
  pending-bag counters are not rewritten as recovery success.
- `src/objectives.cpp`, `src/route_plan.cpp`: add explicit `<cmath>` includes
  required by their inherited `std::ceil` uses on this Pi. No policy changes.
- `README.md`: candidate-specific check command and report link.

New files:

- `src/recovery.h`, `src/recovery.cpp`: owned scalar scene, public backend and
  outcome interface, pure bounded plan selection, channel/path comparison and
  common executor.
- `src/recovery_sdk.h`, `src/recovery_sdk.cpp`: production public-SDK adapter,
  immutable terrain/full home-field cache, membership/range and per-turn action
  history flags, capture and guarded primitive actions.
- `tests/recovery_scenarios.cpp`: scripted backend exercising that same executor
  and planner, without SDK imports or a second decision implementation.
- `tests/run_focused.py`, `tests/source_contracts.py`: runnable Pi checks and
  structural/source-preservation assertions.
- `IMPLEMENTATION.md`: this report.

All other inherited source is byte-identical to the base bot. The source check
verifies this, allowing only the two `<cmath>` include additions above. Original
camp/bank movement, route planning, economics, draft, equipment thresholds,
state selection order and shared communication are retained.

## Interface, ownership and order

`recovery::execute(Intent, Memory&, Backend&) -> Outcome` is the common public
entry. `select_plan(const Scene&, allow_step, allow_dash)` is the pure test seam.
`Scene` owns positions, health, permissions, visibility/occupancy buffers and
scalar threat/camp records. It shares immutable owned static terrain, spawn and
complete home distances. It stores neither live SDK handles nor `observe()`
references. Outcomes carry executed history, successful movement/dash counts,
attempt/cancel/recall/defense/capture/candidate counts, unknown-effect and
prefix-risk rejection counts, plus the homeward-route flag.

Outcomes distinguish channeling (no arrival claim), reached spawn while the
health latch remains set (no healing claim), recovered (health latch released),
partial actions, blocked attempt, no improving motion, defensive/cancelled wait,
incomplete work, initialization deferred and stale epoch. Stale/incomplete
outcomes retain counts/history of actions already completed. A blocked motion
ends the dispatch without another attempt or footer.

The original dead, tribute/teleport, spawn-defense, danger and existing-recall
ordering remains in `decide`. Routing uses the fresh health latch, never
`Facts.recovery` (which also includes gold). Gold-only recall keeps the original
branch outside this adapter. Every escape still uses the controller, including
gold-only evasion; its health footer requires a newly observed health latch.
There is no earlier spawn-healing override. Carried gems do not disable health
recovery; pending bank state survives it.

Controller order:

1. Admit/finish static initialization, capture an owned scene and update the
   inherited <=35% / >=55% health hysteresis.
2. For active recall, compare preservation with a visible, clear, zero-current-
   and-response-exposure path of at most five ordinary steps. Require steps
   <=remaining timer (discounting this turn if known controller movement was
   already spent). Otherwise preserve a clear channel even with distant visible
   enemies. Threatened channels may cancel once through live permission checks.
3. A selected faster-home cancellation refreshes permissions and executes only
   its freshly checked first step. It suppresses new recall for the turn, even
   if that step fails or actual movement after cancellation is unavailable.
4. Otherwise select stay/step/dash/dash-step/step-dash; execute only the first
   action, refresh, update the health latch and replan with remaining allowances.
5. Invoke one guarded compatible defensive primitive, at most once; refresh if
   it acted and update the latch again.
6. Report spawn/recovery truth, or start committed health recall when below
   55%, the latch is set, alive outside spawn, no visible foe or covering awake
   damaging camp/current exposure, and exact permissions/epoch/reserve pass.
   Refresh after starting; channeling does not imply future arrival or healing.

Per-turn native recall-started/cancelled flags and runtime flags block repeat
starts/cancels, including a failed native start. Tribute/teleport are never
cancelled here. Stun, completed-turn, actor/life/round and channel state are
checked explicitly; an empty restriction set is not treated as recall permission.

The defensive adapter retains shield priority at the inherited <70% HP/current
exposure condition, then the inherited ally-heal <75% condition and heal/lethal-
exposure ranking, then one lowest-health reachable enemy basic attack. It is
intentionally a single primitive, not the old multi-action `fight` call: recovery
no longer casts offensive spells/attack resets or follows a shield with another
combat action in this dispatch. It never moves, wakes camps by attacking them,
or starts/cancels channels. Fresh preflight guards issuance; the controller
refreshes before its footer. All ordinary camp-service combat remains unchanged.

## Geometry, effects and bounds

Only integral range 1 or 2, nonexclusive dashes are supported. Nonfinite,
fractional, larger-range, exclusive or otherwise unsupported metadata explicitly
leaves ordinary-step/stay/defense/health-recall fallback. Two simultaneously ready
supported dashes return incomplete rather than silently expanding the cap or
choosing one without comparison. Effect radius support is integral 0..2.

Dash physical paths use one or two eight-neighbor steps through visible,
in-bounds, vacant tiles. Walls, holes, altars, enemy spawn, champions, camps and
teleports block the physical subset. The actual self origin is cleared. There
is no tactical mask in reachability, and no normal-move prerequisite for a
nonexclusive dash. Native allowance/cooldown/restrictions are rechecked before
issuance. Cross-hole or occupied overflight and all exclusive dashes remain
unsupported; no exclusivity inference is made from `!can_move`.

Current basic exposure sums visible enemy and known awake camp Strength in
geometric attack range. Enemy range+1 exposure is separate. Neither is predicted
HP loss: no shield discount, cooldown prediction, beneficial stun or kill is
invented. Each action prefix must have current exposure <=the fresh origin's.
Intermediate nonzero exposure is allowed.

Damage/stun landings require the entire in-bounds effect square visible. All
enemy contacts are initially unsupported because retaliation/passive effects
are not simulated. Each hit camp group requires fresh live/dead evidence for
every member. Positive-damage hits add known living asleep damaging siblings
at full Strength, even when the hit member was already awake or passive.
Groups are deduplicated before siblings are added. Unknown groups/members and
stun-only camp contacts are excluded. A remembered camp tile being visible is
necessary but not sufficient for death evidence; fresh public `state()` must
confirm dead. Missing/hidden state stays unknown.

Membership comes from World's cached groups, never per-endpoint
`camp::camp_group()`. Camp range is cached by public camp kind. Each refresh
captures visible camp positions once, then live state/Strength only for camps
within range+5 of self or in a potentially hit group. This covers the entire
motion neighborhood and five-step channel comparison. Hidden members remain
unknown. Effect/group results are cached once per landing. Scalar current,
response and nearest-enemy features are precomputed on the local 7x7 square;
continuations use those records, with no host getter or `is_set()` in endpoint,
ranking, effect or BFS loops.

Ranking is terminal current exposure, terminal enemy range+1 exposure, full
static physical home distance (65535 remains unreachable), greater nearest
visible-enemy distance, worst action-prefix exposure, motion action count,
then stable first x/y/action and terminal x/y ties. Stay participates, so a
non-improving scene does not force motion.

Explicit caps (`recovery::Limits`):

| Work/data | Limit |
| --- | ---: |
| Map/export cells | 16,384 |
| Visible enemies / defensive allies | 32 each |
| Cached/visible camp records | 256 |
| Cached groups | 128 |
| Ability slots | 2 |
| Ready supported dash choices | 1; more returns incomplete |
| Public query batches between captures | 4,096 |
| Raw plans per selection | 417 including stay; no dedup required |
| Selections per ordinary dispatch | 2, at most 834 raw choices |
| Distinct local effect landing caches | 49 per selection |
| Effect footprint | at most 25 in-bounds tiles per landing |
| Safe-home BFS | depth <=5, 121 nodes, 968 neighbor checks |
| Owned captures per dispatch | 6 maximum |
| Motion | <=2 successes, <=1 ordinary attempt and <=1 dash attempt |
| Channel cancellation / new recall / defense | <=1 each |

Membership matching is bounded by 256x256 scalar handle comparisons per capture.
Feature/effect work is bounded by the record and local-square caps; it performs
no host queries. BFS marks each eligible tile before scoring it, avoiding
repeated threat scans for exposed tiles. Caps and exhausted reserve yield
incomplete, never a partially collected "safe" model. The query cap counts
checked public call batches, not raw engine imports: some SDK methods and
round/fuel checks issue additional host calls. It is not a measured fuel bound.

The home field consumes one admission in the existing shared `TurnBudget`,
using unchanged reserve=5,000, admission=30,000 and total max_fields=3. It uses
full `distance_field::compute` with static blockers and own spawn roots, exports
once, and is reused across turns/lives of this bot instance. It is not a dynamic
or origin-stopped field. No model-dependent action occurs before initialization
finishes. A complete static computation/export that spans an epoch is retained;
the old dispatch then returns stale and discards its dynamic scene. Partial
field data is never published.

Epoch checks surround checked capture/preflight batches, pure planning/BFS and
issuance. Successful native work is counted once before checking for rollover.
There is no unbounded restart in the dispatch. Current-round unexpected native
errors propagate to the existing outer error reporter. Only explicitly missing
camp information is converted to unknown. No new release trace or extra debug
queries are enabled; counters are returned without per-action printing.

## Checks actually run on Pi

Host: aarch64, GCC 13.3.0. From repository root:

```sh
python3 bots/pi_actor-turn-core-01/tests/run_focused.py
```

Result: **292 recovery assertions passed**, inherited protocol/state scenarios
passed, all production source syntax passed, and integration contracts passed.

## Gaps and PC validation

No `uv`/`cambc` or WASI compiler was available on this Pi. Production code received
current-SDK source syntax checks, not an engine-linked/WASM build or gameplay
execution. Scenario scenes are deliberately bounded geometric/control fixtures,
not replay-prefix reproduction or proof of native endpoint acceptance. Scripted
failures/rollovers exercise the same controller contract; actual SDK suspension,
native permission failures, field persistence across real rollover, action-event
ordering, resource cap hits and fuel cost remain unverified in-engine. Full
source/native-backend integration cannot establish the SDK metadata conversion
or native action legality by itself.

In particular, range+1 exposure remains a heuristic and does not certify safety;
Heart599-style beneficial stun cases may be rejected; wider wake effects are
penalized; hole-crossing Heart147 is outside the supported physical subset.
The simplified single-primitive recovery defense may change combat strength.
No attempt was made to fit thresholds, economic utility, carrier-specific
recovery policy or champion strength. Hidden threats and future path safety are
not observed. Query/candidate bounds and reserve checks do not make multiple
actions atomic or guarantee they fit in a turn.

PC should build with the current SDK, run the separately specified frozen
8-game Swirl/Lanes/Elkring/Guardians panel, both sides versus C02, and inspect
native errors, sequences, recovery/arrival/healing, delivery, fuel, rollover and
cap hits. The subsequent economic-core construction should depend on review
and those findings, not a standalone win threshold.
